editorial.headline: A Clear Bali Route for Specialist Financial Services
editorial.standfirst: Specialist financial services—from hedging to own-name digital assets—are nationally open to PMA, and the stated Large-scale risk position leaves the activity outside Bali’s moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 64999 is a deliberately wide home for specialist financial-services work not classified elsewhere. Its stated scope includes financial vehicle corporations other than securitisation; the writing of swaps and options; and other hedging arrangements. It also covers transactions that securitise assets other than loans by issuing financial instruments. A further strand is the issuance, in a business’s own name, of digital financial assets and their associated liabilities—crypto assets are the example given. The scope then reaches other financial services not otherwise covered and financial-sector technology innovation.

The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses. This is meaningful breadth, but it should be read as a scale position rather than as a promise about any particular financial product or operating model. A company belongs within the activity where its actual work fits the recorded scope: a financial vehicle corporation, hedging arrangements, the stated asset transactions, own-name digital assets and their liabilities, or financial-sector technology innovation. For founders, that makes the description a practical boundary: its range is broad, yet its subject matter is specific.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, a foreign investor can hold all of the ownership permitted under this classification at national level. The national result is not qualified in the record by a lower foreign-equity cap. That clarity matters before turning to the province: national foreign ownership and Bali’s local registration treatment are separate parts of the picture, and each must be read from its own recorded field.

In Bali, the honest answer is still open, not blocked. The province’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. For this activity, OSS places the Besar scale at Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—so the moratorium does not block it. Bali’s status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. A foreign-owned company can therefore register this activity in Bali today, while the national 100% ceiling remains the foreign-ownership limit stated in the record.
